data.name: Serment - Contract with a Devil
data.detailed_description:
Serment - Contract with a Devil (or Serment, for short) is a visual novel - dungeon crawler hybrid where you play as a girl who was revived by a beautiful devil.

Though, instead of claiming our heroine’s ever so cliche human soul, the devil demands a huge sum of money for payment. If the payment comes even one day late, the heroine's soul will return to the afterlife.

And so, her light-hearted, comedic adventure to save up enough money before the deadline begins.

Despite the dark sounding premise, the majority of Serment will be light-hearted slice of life events (more commonly known as cute girls doing cute things).

Game features:

  • Cute anime girls!
  • 4 playable main characters, each with their own unique story and endings.
  • More than 10 side characters, each with their own personalities and subplots.
  • A dungeon crawler with manually designed puzzles and 100+ unique items to discover!
  • A lot of cute anime girls!
  • Turn-based RPG battles with simple mechanics but tons of depth.
  • A detailed dating sim time management system.
  • Cooking, crafting and fishing minigames!
  • Light yuri (GxG) romance.
  • Steam Achievements and Trading Cards.
  • Did we mention that there will be cute anime girls?

reviews.review:
Serment - Contract with a Devil is an ambitious independent RPG that mixes visual novel storytelling with first-person dungeon exploration to create a surprisingly memorable adventure. Developed by Nkt Studio and published by Sekai Project, the game begins with an attention-grabbing premise: a young woman is revived after death through a pact with a devil, only to learn that her second chance at life comes with a steep price. She has a limited amount of time to settle her supernatural debt before the consequences catch up to her. While the setup hints at a grim and serious tale, Serment quickly establishes itself as a lighter and more character-focused experience, balancing fantasy themes with humor, friendship, and everyday activities.

Much of the game's appeal lies in its cast. Rather than centering on a single protagonist, players gradually become acquainted with several heroines, each with their own personalities, motivations, and narrative paths. The story embraces familiar anime conventions, but it does so with enough sincerity that the interactions remain enjoyable. Character events are plentiful, and the inclusion of multiple endings encourages players to revisit the game to uncover alternative outcomes. Fans of relationship-driven visual novels will appreciate how much time is devoted to developing bonds between characters, particularly through its light romantic elements and numerous side events.

Outside of its narrative, Serment offers a traditional dungeon-crawling experience viewed from a first-person perspective. The handcrafted dungeons are among the game's strongest features, as they are filled with hidden items, environmental puzzles, and enemies that require more than simple button-mashing to overcome. Exploration feels rewarding thanks to a generous assortment of equipment and collectibles scattered throughout the adventure. The decision to avoid randomly generated maps pays off, as each dungeon feels intentionally designed with its own layout and progression. Puzzle segments provide occasional breaks from combat, helping maintain variety across lengthy play sessions.

Combat follows a turn-based structure that is approachable without becoming completely mindless. Party members possess distinct abilities, encouraging players to experiment with different combinations and strategies. Managing resources becomes increasingly important during extended dungeon expeditions, especially when healing items are limited and stronger enemies begin appearing more frequently. Although veterans of the genre may find the mechanics somewhat straightforward, the system remains entertaining throughout the game's runtime and complements the dungeon-crawling elements effectively.

One of Serment's more interesting additions is its life simulation aspect. Players are not solely focused on clearing dungeons and advancing the plot; they are also responsible for managing their time wisely. Activities such as cooking, fishing, and crafting offer useful rewards while contributing to the game's relaxed atmosphere. Choosing how to spend each day creates an enjoyable balance between progressing the main objective and strengthening relationships with companions. The looming deadline tied to the protagonist's contract gives these decisions additional weight, ensuring that the time management mechanics feel meaningful rather than tacked on.

The presentation is modest but charming. Character artwork is expressive and suits the game's overall tone, while the soundtrack provides a pleasant backdrop for both quiet conversations and dangerous dungeon excursions. Although the production values are understandably limited compared to larger RPGs, Serment demonstrates a clear artistic identity that remains consistent from beginning to end. Its anime-inspired aesthetic will not appeal to everyone, but players who enjoy visual novels and Japanese role-playing games will likely feel right at home.

That said, the game is not without flaws. The pacing can occasionally drag due to lengthy conversations, and some dungeon segments overstay their welcome. Certain gameplay systems, particularly the side activities, feel somewhat underdeveloped and could have benefited from additional depth. Likewise, players who are not fond of anime tropes may struggle to connect with the cast and storytelling approach. However, these shortcomings do little to overshadow the game's strengths, especially considering the scope of what Nkt Studio set out to accomplish.

Serment - Contract with a Devil succeeds because it confidently combines multiple genres into a cohesive package. It may not revolutionize visual novels or dungeon crawlers individually, but its blend of storytelling, exploration, character interactions, and life simulation creates an experience that feels distinct within the indie RPG landscape. For players seeking a lengthy adventure with memorable characters and a mixture of gameplay styles, it offers plenty of value and a surprisingly heartfelt journey beneath its supernatural premise.

Rating: 7/10
